title.narrative: Community Managed Irrigated Agriculture Sector Project

description.narrative: The Project aims to improve the agriculture productivity and sustainability of existing small and medium farmer-managed irrigation systems suffering from low productivity and poverty in Central and Eastern Development Regions thereby enhancing the livelihoods of the poor. This is achieved through (i) providing improved means for WUA empowerment, irrigation infrastructure, agriculture extension, and targeted livelihood enhancement to build the human capital of the poor; and (ii) strengthening policies, plans institutions and their operations for more responsive service delivery and sustainable impacts.

title.narrative: Reports and Recommendations of the President

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: 1 - Farmers in subproject areas have improved irrigation infrastructure. Indicator: 75% of new field-level water courses recommended in ICWM plans are constructed by farmers. Achievement: 28 Progress/Status: Farmers Field School (FFS) has been implemented in 96 ISPs, and infrastructure construction activities have been carried out in 28 ISPs by the farmers.
Data Source: DOWRI' monitoring and evaluation reports

Output: 1 - Farmers in subproject areas have improved irrigation infrastructure. Indicator: By 2021: 35,597 ha of irrigated area is improved (baseline = 0) Achievement: 41621 Progress/Status: The CMIASP-AF set the target of providing improved irrigation services to 19,920 ha. To meet this target, 163 FMIS (20,101 ha) and 6 AMIS (5,465 ha) are approved for project financing. The completion of system improvement work provided improved irrigation services to 26,566 ha which is more than what was expected during the project design.
Infrastructure improvement works have been completed in 111 ISPs under CMIASP and 162 FMIS and 6 AMIS ISPs under AF providing improved irrigation services to 41,621 ha. (15,677 ha from CMIASP and 25,944 ha under CMIASP-AF).
Data Source: DOWRI's monitoring and evaluation reports

Output: 2 - WUAs independently manage irrigation systems in a socially inclusive and equitable manner. Indicator: By 2021: 100% of subproject WUAs are active. Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: In all 168 ISPs of batch-I, II, III and AMIS, WUAs have been formed and duly registered. The assessment of WUA shows that above 150 are active with a form system of resource mobilization, ISF collection in 100 ISPs in regular basis, permanent WUA staff member (61 ISPs) responsible for water distribution, recurrent maintenance in regular basis. The EA is further assessing the above details and will soon report the updated data. Data Source: DOWRI's review of WUA meeting minutes at project end.

Output: 2 - WUAs independently manage irrigation systems in a socially inclusive and equitable manner. Indicator: Recommended integrated crop and water management plans are adopted by at least 80% of WUAs. Achievement: 20 Progress/Status: The project has organized SP-specific O&M plan formulation with WUA. The project recruited 5 Agri engineers who worked with WUA and assisted them in preparing system-specific canal O&M plans. The EA is further assessing the above details and will soon report the updated data. Data Source: DOWRI's end-of-project survey.

Output: 2 - WUAs independently manage irrigation systems in a socially inclusive and equitable manner. Indicator: WUA committees have at least 33% women Achievement: 38 Progress/Status: The governance structure of WUA is fairly inclusive. The Overall representation of women is 38% whereas 75% of WUAs have one or more woman holding key leadership position. The EA is further assessing the above details and will soon report the updated data. Data Source: WUA general assembly minutes. DOWRI's end-of-project survey.

Output: 2 - WUAs independently manage irrigation systems in a socially inclusive and equitable manner. Indicator: With at least 50% of WUAs having a woman in a leadership position. Data Source: DOWRI's end-of-project survey. Actual value:

Output: 3 - Farmers adopt improved agricultural practices. Indicator: 40% of farmer group members trained are women. Achievement: 57 Progress/Status: 57% of the total trainees of commodity-based agriculture extension program are female Data Source: DOAD end-of-project report.
Output: 3 - Farmers adopt improved agricultural practices. Indicator: Among the certified farmer, 35% of leader farmers are women. Achievement: 23 Data Source: DOAD end-of-project report.

Output: 3 - Farmers adopt improved agricultural practices. Indicator: At least one leader farmer is certified in each subproject Achievement: 150 Progress/Status: One participant from each subproject have been provided with leader farmer training of which 54% are women. In total, nearly 150 lead farmers have been trained. Data Source: DOAD end-of-project report.

Output: 3 - Farmers adopt improved agricultural practices. Indicator: By 2021: Seed replacement rate of major crops is increased to 13% Achievement: 18.13 Progress/Status: The initial result indicates that 18.13% seed replacement rate has been acheived in the completed subprojects. The indication so far is the Project will achieve the target. Data Source: DOAD end-of-project report.

Output: 2 - WUAs independently manage irrigation systems in a socially inclusive and equitable manner. Indicator: Funding and implementation mechanism for O&M is in place for all WUAs. Achievement: Yes Progress/Status: The analysis of the O&M practices adopted by the WUAs revealed that majority of WUAs (150 out of 168) have functional and effective system of O&M and are raising ISF on need basic. The 100 WUAs are regularly raising ISF with an average rate of NRs. 1400/ha./year. The labor mobilization for recurrent maintenance of 150 WUAs showed that average mobilization for maintenance requirement around 228-person day/year. Similarly, 61 WUAs have appointed paid staff for canal operation and are paying in average NRs.55,664 per year/staff. The EA is further assessing the above details and will soon report the updated data. Data Source: DOWRI's end-of-project survey. Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Target year: 2021 Target value: Y Actual value: Yes

Output: 2 - WUAs independently manage irrigation systems in a socially inclusive and equitable manner. Indicator: WUA committees have equitable representation from head, middle, and tail of irrigation system. Achievement: Yes Progress/Status: The executive committees have been noted fairly inclusive with representation from the head, middle and tail of the canal system. The representation stands at 26% from head reach, 41% from the middle and 33% from the tail reach of the system. The EA is further assessing the above details and will soon report the updated data. Data Source: WUA general assembly minutes. Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Target year: 2021 Target value: Y Actual value: Yes

Output: 4 - National institutions are strengthened for effective irrigation service delivery. Indicator: By 2021: Project outputs delivered on time and within budget. Achievement: Y Progress/Status: 111 FMIS ISPs completed under CMIASP (6 partially completed) and 163 FMIS ISPs under CMIASP-AF have been completed on time and within budget. Also, 6 AMIS have been completed and handed over to farmer's WUAs. Overall physical progress of the project is 99%. Data Source: Project contract awards and disbursements data. Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Target year: 2021 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: 4 - National institutions are strengthened for effective irrigation service delivery. Indicator: DOI association organizers improved their inclusive service delivery in subproject areas. Achievement: Y Progress/Status: DOI association organizers worked with WUAs of all 111 ISPs under CMIASP to mobilize farmers. Their service has remained same in the Batch I, II and III ISPs under CMIASP-AF. Both availability of AO in the division offices and the quality of their service requires improvement. Data Source: WUA assessment of association organizers' service at project end. Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Target year: 2021 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: 4 - National institutions are strengthened for effective irrigation service delivery. Indicator: Planned reforms are implemented. Achievement: Y Progress/Status: - Irrigation Policy was approved by the government on 2013. Again, new policy considering federal structure is under preparation. - IWRM policy was drafted. DOI mission and vision document prepared. - DOI new organizational restructuring completed. - Irrigation act is drafted, approved by the Cabinet and is currently under review by the Parliament. - Government is also drafting an integrated water resource act. - MOI is reorganized as Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation. DOI under federal ministry is converted in to DOWRI. IDDs under DOI in the center is converted into WRIDDs under provinces. DADOs have been dissolved and converted in to Agriculture Knowledge Center under provinces. Data Source: MOWRI's annual reports. Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2013 Baseline value: N Target year: 2021 Target value: Y Actual value: Y
Participating farmers increase agricultural production.

By 2021: Yields of each major crop increased by at least 30% in subproject areas (baselines reported in SPPRs) Achievement: 38.9 Progress/Status: PBME Survey conducted in 81 CMIASP-AF ISPs, indicate that yield is increased by 38.9% (irrespective of crops). Data Source: DOWRI project completion report.

Cropping intensity in irrigated areas is increased to at least 199% in hill subprojects (baseline 2013: 154%). Achievement: 227.3 Progress/Status: The overall cropping intensity of sub-projects after the project intervention in hills is 227.3%. Data Source: SPPRs for baseline data, with postconstruction survey.

Cropping intensity in irrigated areas is increased to at least 188% in Terai subprojects (baseline 2013: 158%). Achievement: 219.5 Progress/Status: The overall cropping intensity of sub-projects after the project intervention in Terai is 219.5%. Data Source: SPPRs for baseline data, with postconstruction survey.
